points.m: Explains the cause or reason why something is. [Because ...]
points.form: Main Sentence んです。
points.note: Use んです to give a reason as an answer, or to add the reason or cause for what you just stated. (～のです → ～んです)
ex: どうして遅れたんですか。
Why were you late?
電車が遅れたんです。
Because the train was late.
どうしたんですか。
What's the matter?
頭が痛いんです。
Because my head hurts.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Explains the cause or reason why something is. [Because ...]
o: V て-form いただけませんか。
q.e: Use んです to give a reason as an answer, or to add the reason or cause for what you just stated. (～のです → ～んです)

points.m: Using んです in question form.
points.form: Main Sentence んですか。
points.note: Use it when the speaker guesses the reason or cause of something and confirms whether it is correct, or asks for information about what he or she has seen or heard.
ex: 山口さん、英語が上手ですね。外国に住んでいたんですか。
Ms. Yamaguchi, you speak very good English. Have you lived abroad?
毎日晩ごはんを作りますか。
Do you cook dinner every day?
いいえ、時間がないんです。
No, (because) I don't have time.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Using んです in question form.
o: V て-form いただけませんか。
q.e: Use it when the speaker guesses the reason or cause of something and confirms whether it is correct, or asks for information about what he or she has seen or heard.

points.m: Introducing a topic before a request or invitation.
points.form: ～んですが、～。
points.note: Use ～んですが to set the scene first, and then make your request, question or invitation in the second part.
ex: お金がないんですが、明日はらってもいいですか。
Umm.. I have no money, is it okay to pay tomorrow?
わたしもクリスティーナさんのパーティーへ行くんですが、いっしょに行きませんか。
Umm.. I'm also going to Kristina's birthday party, do you want to go together?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Introducing a topic before a request or invitation.
o: V て-form いただけませんか。
q.e: Use ～んですが to set the scene first, and then make your request, question or invitation in the second part.

points.m: Could you please ...? / Would you please do me the favor of ~ing?
points.form: V て-form いただけませんか。
points.note: A very polite way to ask someone to do something for you. Use the て-form of the verb followed by いただけませんか。
ex: やり方が分からないんですが、教えていただけませんか。
I don't know how to do it, could you please teach me?
レポートを終わりました。出す前に見ていただけませんか。
I finished the report. Could you please check it before I submit it?
そちらで電話をわすれましたが、さがしていただけませんか。
I forgot my phone there. Could you please search it for me?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Could you please ...? / Would you please do me the favor of ~ing?
o: V て-form いただけませんか。
q.e: A very polite way to ask someone to do something for you. Use the て-form of the verb followed by いただけませんか。

points.m: What / When / Where / Which / How / Who should I ...?
points.form: V た-formら いいですか。
points.note: Use a question word with Vたらいいですか to ask for advice or instructions about what you should do.
ex: おなかがすいた。どこで食べたらいいですか。
I'm hungry, where should I eat?
おみやげを買いたいんですが、何を買ったらいいですか。
I want to buy Japanese souvenirs, what should I buy?
パスポートをなくなりましたが、どうしたらいいですか。
I lost my passport, what should I do?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: What / When / Where / Which / How / Who should I ...?
o: V た-formら いいですか。
q.e: Use a question word with Vたらいいですか to ask for advice or instructions about what you should do.

points.m: The object particle が is replaced by the topic particle は.
points.form: N (object) は 好きです・きらいです / 上手です・下手です / あります
points.note: が: the subject is the unknown (new information). は: the predicate is the unknown, so the noun becomes the topic.
ex: くだものは好きじゃないと思います。
Is it better to give her fruits? / I think she doesn't like fruits.
ごめん、スポーツは上手じゃないんです。
Let's play basketball. / Sorry, I'm not good with sports.
いいえ、テストはあります。
Don't we have a test today? / Yes, we have a test.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: The object particle が is replaced by the topic particle は.
o: N (object) は 好きです・きらいです / 上手です・下手です / あります
q.e: が: the subject is the unknown (new information). は: the predicate is the unknown, so the noun becomes the topic.

points.m: Verbs expressing the ability to do something: "can" or "be able to".
points.form: Verb ます-stem → える／られる + ます
points.note: Group 1: change the last sound to the え-row (書きます → 書けます). Group 2: add られ (食べます → 食べられます). Group 3: 来ます → こられます, します → できます.
ex: 書きます → 書けます
I can write.
買います → 買えます
I can buy.
食べます → 食べられます
I can eat.
します → できます
I can do it.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Verbs expressing the ability to do something: "can" or "be able to".
o: Verb ます-stem → える／られる + ます
q.e: Group 1: change the last sound to the え-row (書きます → 書けます). Group 2: add られ (食べます → 食べられます). Group 3: 来ます → こられます, します → できます.

points.m: The object particle を usually changes to が in a potential sentence.
points.form: N を V → N が V (potential)
points.note: The thing you are able to do is marked with が. Other particles such as へ and に stay the same.
ex: わたしは英語を話します。→ わたしは英語が話せます。
I speak English. → I can speak English.
一人でくうこうへ行けますか。
Can you go to the airport alone?
明日6時に起きられますか。
Can you wake up at six tomorrow morning?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: The object particle を usually changes to が in a potential sentence.
o: N を V → N が V (potential)
q.e: The thing you are able to do is marked with が. Other particles such as へ and に stay the same.

points.p: 見えます / 聞こえます
points.m: Something can be seen or heard (naturally comes into sight or hearing).
points.form: N が 見えます ／ N が 聞こえます
points.note: 見えます (can be seen) and 聞こえます (can be heard) are used for things that come into view or earshot. 見られます / 聞けます mean you are able to watch / listen.
ex: 明日からその映画が見られます。
You can watch the movie starting tomorrow.
この町からふじ山が見えます。
Mt. Fuji can be seen from this town.
オーディオガイドで説明が聞けます。
You can listen to the explanation using this audio guide.
あの部屋からふしぎな音が聞こえます。
A strange sound can be heard from that room.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something can be seen or heard (naturally comes into sight or hearing).
o: N が 見えます ／ N が 聞こえます
q.e: 見えます (can be seen) and 聞こえます (can be heard) are used for things that come into view or earshot. 見られます / 聞けます mean you are able to watch / listen.

points.p: では・には・へは・からは・までは
points.m: は is added after another particle to highlight or emphasize a noun as a topic.
points.form: N + particle + は
points.note: Place は after particles like で, に, へ, から, まで to put the focus on that place or point.
ex: へやにはテレビがあります。
In the room, there is a TV.
店ではさけが買えます。
At the store, you can buy Japanese wine.
このビルからは花火が見えます。
From this building, fireworks can be seen.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: は is added after another particle to highlight or emphasize a noun as a topic.
q.e: Place は after particles like で, に, へ, から, まで to put the focus on that place or point.

points.m: Also / too.
points.form: N も ～。
points.note: も replaces は, が or を to say that the same thing applies to another noun. It can also follow other particles (リビングルームにも).
ex: サラダを食べました。ケーキも食べました。
I ate salad. I also ate a cake.
しみずさんは英語が話せます。中国語も話せます。
Mr. Shimizu can speak English. He can also speak Chinese.
へやにはテレビがあります。リビングルームにもテレビがあります。
In the room, there is a TV. Also in the living room, there is a TV.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Also / too.
q.e: も replaces は, が or を to say that the same thing applies to another noun. It can also follow other particles (リビングルームにも).

points.m: Only / just / nothing but ...
points.form: N しか + negative verb
points.note: しか is always followed by a negative: there is nothing but N. だけ + positive gives a similar meaning of "only".
ex: コピーは一つしかありません。
I have nothing but just one copy.
コピーは一つだけあります。
I only have one copy.
かのじょしか買ってあげない。
I won't buy it for anyone but (only) her.
かのじょだけに買ってあげる。
I'll buy it only for her.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Only / just / nothing but ...
q.e: しか is always followed by a negative: there is nothing but N. だけ + positive gives a similar meaning of "only".

points.m: Doing Verb 1 while doing Verb 2.
points.form: Verb 1 ます-stem ながら Verb 2
points.note: Drop ます from Verb 1 and add ながら. The main action is the verb at the end of the sentence.
ex: わらいながらおもしろいばんぐみを見ました。
I was laughing while watching a funny show.
アルバイトをやりながら大学で勉強します。
I'm working part time and studying in university.
本を書きながら英語を教えました。
I was writing a book while I was teaching English.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Doing Verb 1 while doing Verb 2.
o: Verb 1 ます-stem ながら Verb 2
q.e: Drop ます from Verb 1 and add ながら. The main action is the verb at the end of the sentence.

points.m: An action done habitually, repeated over time.
points.form: Verb ています ／ Verb ていました
points.note: Use the て-form + います for a habit in the present, and ていました for a habit in the past.
ex: 毎朝、ごはんを食べる前にジョギングをしています。
I jog every morning before breakfast.
土日はせんたくしています。
I do the laundry on Saturdays and Sundays.
毎晩ビールを飲んでいました。
I drank beer every night.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: An action done habitually, repeated over time.
o: Verb ています ／ Verb ていました
q.e: Use the て-form + います for a habit in the present, and ていました for a habit in the past.

points.m: Describing something using more than one adjective, or stating more than one reason.
points.form: Plain form し、～。
points.note: Join verbs or adjectives in plain form with し to list several facts or reasons, one on top of another.
ex: 姉のアパートは新しいし、にわもあります。
My sister's apartment is new and it also has a garden.
好きな人はやさしいし、きれいだし、人気があります。
My crush is kind, beautiful and popular.
かのじょは英語が話せるし、ねっしんだし、けいけんもあります。
She can speak English, is earnest and also has experience.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Describing something using more than one adjective, or stating more than one reason.
q.e: Join verbs or adjectives in plain form with し to list several facts or reasons, one on top of another.

points.m: Refusing politely by giving reasons; also implies more than one reason (among other things).
points.form: Plain form し、Plain form し。
points.note: The particle も can be used with し to hint that there are other reasons as well.
ex: ごめん、母をてつだうし、レポートをやらなければならない。
Would you like to have coffee later? / Sorry, I have to help my mother and I have to do my report.
駅からも近いし、このマンションを買います。
It's also near the station. I'll buy this condominium.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Refusing politely by giving reasons; also implies more than one reason (among other things).
o: Plain form し、Plain form し。
q.e: The particle も can be used with し to hint that there are other reasons as well.

points.m: Besides, moreover (adding one more point).
points.form: ～し、～し、それに ～。
points.note: それに adds a further reason or point on top of the ones already given.
ex: ジムがあるし、安いし、それに駅からも近いです。
Why did you choose that condominium? / It has a gym, it's cheap, and besides, it's close to the station.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Besides, moreover (adding one more point).
q.e: それに adds a further reason or point on top of the ones already given.

points.m: Then / so / and that's why...
points.form: ～し、～し。それで ～。
points.note: それで begins a new sentence that states the result of the reasons given before.
ex: かのじょは英語が話せるし、ねっしんだし、けいけんもあります。それで社長はガルシアさんをえらびました。
She can speak English, is earnest and has experience. That's why the company president chose Ms. Garcia.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Then / so / and that's why...
q.e: それで begins a new sentence that states the result of the reasons given before.

points.m: Both へ and に can mark the place you are going to.
points.form: Place へ...(direction) ・ Place に...(destination)
points.note: With verbs of movement (go, come, go home, go on a business trip), the destination can be marked with へ or に.
ex: よくこのきっさてんに来るんですか。
Do you often come to this coffee shop?
へ・に行きます ／ へ・に帰ります
go / go home
へ・に来ます ／ へ・にしゅっちょうします
come / go on a business trip
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Both へ and に can mark the place you are going to.
q.e: With verbs of movement (go, come, go home, go on a business trip), the destination can be marked with へ or に.

points.m: Describes the current state of something (a state that results from a change).
points.form: N が・は Verb て-form います
points.note: Use the て-form + います with が or は to describe how something is right now. Verbs like 開く, われる, こわれる and やぶれる are used this way.
ex: ドアが開いています。
The door is open.
まどがわれています。
The window is broken.
このじどうはんばいきはこわれています。
This vending machine is broken.
あのふくろはやぶれています。
That bag is torn.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Describes the current state of something (a state that results from a change).
o: N が・は Verb て-form います
q.e: Use the て-form + います with が or は to describe how something is right now. Verbs like 開く, われる, こわれる and やぶれる are used this way.

points.p: ～てしまいました / ～てしまいます
points.m: Emphasizes the completion of an action (finished it completely).
points.form: Verb て-form しまいました ／ しまいます
points.note: Use the て-form + しまいました for something already finished, and しまいます for something you will finish by a certain time.
ex: いのうえさんがくれたケーキは全部食べてしまいました。
I ate all the cake that Mr. Inoue gave me.
しゅくだいはもうやってしまいましたか。
Have you done your homework already?
帰る時間までにレポートを書いてしまいます。
I will finish writing the report by the time I leave.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Emphasizes the completion of an action (finished it completely).
o: Verb て-form しまいました ／ しまいます
q.e: Use the て-form + しまいました for something already finished, and しまいます for something you will finish by a certain time.

points.m: Expresses embarrassment or regret about something that happened.
points.form: Verb て-form しまいました。
points.note: The same form is used when something happened by mistake or against your wishes, such as losing or forgetting something.
ex: きっぷをなくしてしまいましたが。どうしたらいいですか。
I lost my train ticket. What should I do?
まちがえてしまいました。もういっかいやります。
I made a mistake. I'll do it one more time.
人が多かったです。それでスピーチをわすれてしまいました。
There were so many people. That's why I forgot my speech.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Expresses embarrassment or regret about something that happened.
o: Verb て-form しまいました。
q.e: The same form is used when something happened by mistake or against your wishes, such as losing or forgetting something.

points.p: どこかで / どこかに
points.m: Somewhere.
points.form: どこかで ～ ／ どこかに ～
points.note: Add か to どこ to say "somewhere". Keep the particle (で or に) that the verb needs after it.
ex: 何か言いたいことがあります。どこかで話せますか。
There's something I want to tell you, can we talk somewhere?
母はそうじしたとき、いいおさらがどこかにかたづけました。
When my mother was cleaning, the nice plates were put away somewhere.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Somewhere.
o: どこかで ～ ／ どこかに ～
q.e: Add か to どこ to say "somewhere". Keep the particle (で or に) that the verb needs after it.

points.m: Found it! (something you were looking for turned up).
points.form: N が ありました。
points.note: Use ありました when you find something you were looking for.
ex: きっぷがありました。おとしましたよ。
I found the ticket. I had dropped it!
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Found it! (something you were looking for turned up).
o: N が ありました。
q.e: Use ありました when you find something you were looking for.

points.m: Something has been done intentionally (and remains that way).
points.form: N2 は N1 に V て-form あります。
points.note: Use the て-form + あります to describe the result of something someone did on purpose. The thing done is the topic (は).
ex: にんぎょうはたなにかざってあります。
The doll has been displayed on the shelf.
ごみばこはすみにおいてあります。
The trash bin has been put in the corner.
ホッチキスはひきだしにしまってあります。
The stapler has been put away in the drawer.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something has been done intentionally (and remains that way).
o: N2 は N1 に V て-form あります。
q.e: Use the て-form + あります to describe the result of something someone did on purpose. The thing done is the topic (は).

points.m: Something has been done on purpose in preparation for something else.
points.form: もう V て-form あります。
points.note: Add もう (already) to say that the preparation has been done already.
ex: プレゼントはもう買ってあります。
I have already bought the gifts.
パーティーの時間はもうしらせてありますか。
Have they already announced the time of the party?
ホテルはもうよやくしてあります。
I have already reserved a hotel.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something has been done on purpose in preparation for something else.
o: もう V て-form あります。
q.e: Add もう (already) to say that the preparation has been done already.

points.p: 閉めてあります vs 閉まっています
points.m: てあります: someone closed it on purpose. ています: the state of being closed.
points.form: V て-form あります ／ V て-form います
points.note: てあります is used with a transitive verb (someone did it on purpose). ています is used with an intransitive verb to describe the state.
ex: まどが閉めてあります。
The window has been closed.
まどが閉まっています。
The window is closed.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: てあります: someone closed it on purpose. ています: the state of being closed.
o: V て-form あります ／ V て-form います
q.e: てあります is used with a transitive verb (someone did it on purpose). ています is used with an intransitive verb to describe the state.

points.m: Completion of a necessary action by a given time, or in readiness for the next time.
points.form: V て-form おきます。
points.note: Use the て-form + おきます to do something beforehand. It can also mean to keep the current state as it is.
ex: お父さん来る前に部屋をそうじしておいてください。
Clean the room before father comes.
じゅぎょうの前に、よしゅうしておきます。
I will prepare the lesson before the class.
食事が終わったら、おさらはそこにおいてください。
When you've finished the meal, please leave the plates there.
おさらはそこにおいときます。
I will leave the plates there.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Completion of a necessary action by a given time, or in readiness for the next time.
q.e: Use the て-form + おきます to do something beforehand. It can also mean to keep the current state as it is.

points.m: Still ~
points.form: まだ Verb (affirmative)
points.note: Use まだ with an affirmative verb to say that something is still going on.
ex: まだゆきが降っています。
It's still snowing.
どうぐをまだ使っていますから、そのままにしておいてください。
I'm still using the tool so please leave them as is there.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Still ~
q.e: Use まだ with an affirmative verb to say that something is still going on.

points.m: That (the thing you mentioned).
points.form: それは ～
points.note: Use それは to respond to what the other person just said, for example agreeing or politely declining.
ex: ブロードウェイでミュージカルを見たいです。→ それはいいですね。
I want to see a musical on Broadway. / That sounds nice.
お金を貸してもらえますか。→ それはちょっと。。
Can you lend me money? / That will be a bit (difficult).
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: That (the thing you mentioned).
q.e: Use それは to respond to what the other person just said, for example agreeing or politely declining.

points.m: Plain style of ～ましょう (let's ~) and ～ましょうか (shall I ~?).
points.form: Verb ます-form → よう／おう  ・  ～ましょうか → ようか
points.note: Group 1: change the last sound to the お-row + う (買います → 買おう). Group 2: drop ます and add よう (見ます → 見よう). Group 3: 来ます → こよう, します → しよう.
ex: つかれたから、ちょっときゅうけいしよう。
I'm tired so let's take a short break.
よく見えないから、前の方にすわろう。
We can't see it very well so let's sit towards the front.
これ好き？買おうか。
Do you like this? Shall I buy it?
重いですよ。てつだおうか。
It's heavy. Shall I help you?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Plain style of ～ましょう (let's ~) and ～ましょうか (shall I ~?).
o: Verb ます-form → よう／おう  ・  ～ましょうか → ようか
q.e: Group 1: change the last sound to the お-row + う (買います → 買おう). Group 2: drop ます and add よう (見ます → 見よう). Group 3: 来ます → こよう, します → しよう.

points.p: ～と思っています / ～と思います
points.m: I am thinking of doing Verb.
points.form: Verb (volitional form) と思っています。
points.note: Put the volitional form before と思っています to say what you are thinking of doing. 思います is also used.
ex: こどもは大学をそつぎょうしてから、主人と旅行へ行こうと思っています。
After my child graduates from university, I have been thinking of going on a trip with my husband.
家で食べようと思います。
I think I will eat at home.
お兄さんは英語のしけんをうけようと思っています。
My brother is thinking of taking the English exam.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: きっと: surely. たぶん: maybe. もしかしたら: possibly.

points.p: 何か・だれか・どこか・いつか

points.form: N なら、Main Sentence
points.note: Use なら to pick up a topic that was just mentioned and give a suggestion or information about it.
ex: 一週間なら、パラワンかセブがいいと思います。
If it's for a week, I think Palawan or Cebu is good.
おんせんなら、白馬がいいですよ。
If it's for a hot spring, Hakuba is good.
この方法がだめならあの方法でやりましょう。
If this way doesn't work, let's do the other method.
25メートルぐらいならおよげます。
If it's just around 25 meters, I can swim it.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: If you are talking about N, then ...
q.e: Use なら to pick up a topic that was just mentioned and give a suggestion or information about it.

points.m: Where / what / how should I ...?
points.form: Interrogative V ば-form いいですか。
points.note: Use a question word with the ば-form of the verb followed by いいですか to ask for a suggestion or direction.
ex: おそうしきに行くんですが、何を持って行けばいいですか。
I'm going to a funeral but what should I bring?
ともだちがけっこんするんですが、どんな物をあげればいいですか。
My friend is getting married. What kind of thing should I give as a present?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Where / what / how should I ...?
o: Interrogative V ば-form いいですか。
q.e: Use a question word with the ば-form of the verb followed by いいですか to ask for a suggestion or direction.

points.m: The more ..., the more ...
points.form: V ば・なら (V dictionary form / い-adj / な-adj) ほど～
points.note: Repeat the verb or adjective: first in the conditional form, then in the dictionary form, followed by ほど.
ex: にんにくをたくさん入れれば入れるほどおいしいと思います。
I think the more garlic you use, the more delicious it is.
きかいはボタンが少なければ少ないほどいいです。
The less buttons in the machine, the better.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: The more ..., the more ...
o: V ば・なら (V dictionary form / い-adj / な-adj) ほど～
q.e: Repeat the verb or adjective: first in the conditional form, then in the dictionary form, followed by ほど.

points.m: V2 is done in order to V1 (so that V1 happens).
points.form: V1 dictionary form / ない-form ように、V2
points.note: Put the goal (usually a potential verb or a verb that expresses a state) in the dictionary or ない-form before ように, then say what you do to reach it.
ex: 早くとどくようにそくたつで出します。
I will send it by express mail in order for it to be delivered early.
日本で働けるように日本語を勉強します。
I will learn Japanese so that I'll be able to work in Japan.
はっきり聞こえるように大きいこえで言ってください。
Please speak loudly so that you can be heard clearly.
家族がしんぱいしないように電話をかけます。
So that my family will not worry, I will call them.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: V2 is done in order to V1 (so that V1 happens).
o: V1 dictionary form / ない-form ように、V2
q.e: Put the goal (usually a potential verb or a verb that expresses a state) in the dictionary or ない-form before ように, then say what you do to reach it.

points.m: Something changes to a different state; one comes to be able to do or to do something.
points.form: V dictionary form ようになります
points.note: Use the dictionary form (often the potential form) before ようになります to say that something became possible or a new habit was acquired.
ex: 日本語の漢字のビデオを見れば、漢字が読めるようになります。
If you watch kanji videos, you will be able to read kanji.
毎日使っているから、スマホで速くうてるようになりました。
I use it everyday, so I've become able to type fast on my smartphone.
人間は2おく年ぐらい前から肉を食べるようになりました。
Humans started to eat meat from about 2 million years ago.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something changes to a different state; one comes to be able to do or to do something.
o: V dictionary form ようになります
q.e: Use the dictionary form (often the potential form) before ようになります to say that something became possible or a new habit was acquired.

points.m: Something that used to be possible or habitual no longer is.
points.form: V ～なくなります
points.note: Change the ない-form of the verb to なく and add なります to express that a habit or ability which existed before has become obsolete.
ex: ロックダウンだからおおぜいの人がじゆうに出かけられなくなります。
Because of the lockdown, many people won't be able to go out freely.
こどもたちは学校で勉強できなくなりました。
Children can no longer study at school.
パソコンを買ってから、もうテレビを見なくなりました。
Since I bought my computer, I don't watch TV anymore.
もうチョパンのきょくがひけるようになりましたか。
Have you been able to play Chopin's work? / No, not yet.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something that used to be possible or habitual no longer is.
q.e: Change the ない-form of the verb to なく and add なります to express that a habit or ability which existed before has become obsolete.

points.m: I try to do / I try not to do (habitually).
points.form: V dictionary form / ない-form ようにしています
points.note: Use ようにしています to say that you make an ongoing effort to do something, or not to do something, as a habit.
ex: できるだけ、毎日ジョッギングするようにしています。
Only if possible, I try to jog everyday.
できれば、毎月5万円ずつちょきんするようにしています。
If I can, I try to save 50,000 yen per month.
夜にねむれないから、寝る前に電子デバイスを使わないようにしています。
Because I can't fall asleep at night, I try not to use electronic devices before going to bed.
ふとりましたから、おかしを食べないようにしています。
Since I got fat, I try not to eat sweets.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I try to do / I try not to do (habitually).
o: V dictionary form / ない-form ようにしています
q.e: Use ようにしています to say that you make an ongoing effort to do something, or not to do something, as a habit.

points.m: Please try to ~ / Please make sure to ~.
points.form: V dictionary form / ない-form ようにしてください
points.note: Use it to request that someone try to do something habitually and continuously. It can also politely request someone to try to do something in a one-off situation.
ex: きそくをまもるようにしてください。
Please try to follow the rules.
明日はぜったいにおくれないようにしてください。
Please be sure not to be late tomorrow.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Please try to ~ / Please make sure to ~.
o: V dictionary form / ない-form ようにしてください
q.e: Use it to request that someone try to do something habitually and continuously. It can also politely request someone to try to do something in a one-off situation.

points.m: Things like A and B; A, B and so on.
points.form: Aとか Bとか
points.note: Use とか after each item to give examples. It is similar to ～や～など.
ex: そうですね。ダンスとかすいえいとか。。。
What kind of exercise do you do, Ms. Yamanaka? / Well, dancing, swimming and so on.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Things like A and B; A, B and so on.
q.e: Use とか after each item to give examples. It is similar to ～や～など.

points.m: Passive verb form (to be done by someone).
points.form: Group 1: い-row → あ-row + れます / Group 2: られます / Group 3: こられます・されます
points.note: Group 1: change the い-row sound of the ます form to the あ-row and add れます. Group 2: replace ます with られます. Group 3: 来ます → 来られます, します → されます.
ex: たのまれる
to be asked / to be requested (Group 1)
しかられる
to be scolded (Group 1)
ほめられる
to be praised (Group 2)
しょうたいされる
to be invited (Group 3)
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Passive verb form (to be done by someone).
o: Group 1: い-row → あ-row + れます / Group 2: られます / Group 3: こられます・されます
q.e: Group 1: change the い-row sound of the ます form to the あ-row and add れます. Group 2: replace ます with られます. Group 3: 来ます → 来られます, します → されます.

points.m: Person1 got something done by Person2. / Person2 did something to Person1.
points.form: N1 (P1) は N2 (P2) に Passive Verb
points.note: The person affected by the action becomes the topic (は) and the person who does the action is marked by に, followed by the passive verb. Active: 先生はわたしをほめました → Passive: わたしは先生にほめられました。
ex: わたしは犬にかまれました。
I was bitten by a dog.
父にしかられました。
I was scolded by my father.
わたしは母に買い物をたのまれました。
I was asked to go shopping by my mother.
シュさんにパーティーにしょうたいされました。
I was invited to the party by Mr. Hsu.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Person1 got something done by Person2. / Person2 did something to Person1.
o: N1 (P1) は N2 (P2) に Passive Verb
q.e: The person affected by the action becomes the topic (は) and the person who does the action is marked by に, followed by the passive verb. Active: 先生はわたしをほめました → Passive: わたしは先生にほめられました。

points.m: Person2 did something to Person1's belonging, and Person1 is annoyed or troubled by it.
points.form: N1 (P1) は N2 (P2) に N3 を Passive Verb
points.note: Use it when someone does something to your belonging and you are annoyed or troubled by it. Do not use it when you are grateful for what the other person did; use ～てもらいます instead.
ex: わたしは弟にPS4をこわされました。
I got my PS4 broken by my little brother.
わたしはねこに手をかまれました。
I got my hand bitten by a cat.
わたしはどろぼうにカメラをとられました。
I got my camera stolen by a thief.
わたしは前にいる男に足をふまれました。
I got my foot stepped on by the man in front of me.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Person2 did something to Person1's belonging, and Person1 is annoyed or troubled by it.
o: N1 (P1) は N2 (P2) に N3 を Passive Verb
q.e: Use it when someone does something to your belonging and you are annoyed or troubled by it. Do not use it when you are grateful for what the other person did; use ～てもらいます instead.

points.m: A noun (thing) has been done, discovered, exported or held.
points.form: N (thing) が・は Passive Verb
points.note: When the doer is not important, the thing itself becomes the subject or topic and the verb is in the passive form.
ex: フランスでむかしの日本のえがはっけんされました。
An old Japanese painting has been discovered in France.
日本の車は せかいじゅうへ ゆしゅつされています。
Japanese cars are being exported all over the world.
つぎのオリンピックは東京で行なわれます。
The next Olympics is going to be held in Tokyo.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: A noun (thing) has been done, discovered, exported or held.
q.e: When the doer is not important, the thing itself becomes the subject or topic and the verb is in the passive form.

points.m: N1 was created, invented or discovered by N2.
points.form: N1 (thing) は N2 (person) によって Passive Verb
points.note: Use によって instead of に to show the person who created, invented or discovered something.
ex: ダビデのちょうこくはミケランジェロによってほられました。
The statue of David was sculpted by Michelangelo.
電話はベルによってはつめいされました。
The telephone was invented by Bell.
このワクチンは日本の理学者によってはっけんされました。
This vaccine was discovered by a Japanese scientist.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: N1 was created, invented or discovered by N2.
o: N1 (thing) は N2 (person) によって Passive Verb
q.e: Use によって instead of に to show the person who created, invented or discovered something.

points.p: から・で つくられます
points.m: N1 is made from / of N2.
points.form: N1 は N2 から・で つくられます
points.note: Use から when the original material changes form (beer from barley), and で when the material is still recognizable (a house made of wood).
ex: ビールはむぎからつくられます。
Beer is made from barley.
むかし、日本の家はぜんぶ木でつくられました。
In the past, Japanese houses were all made of wood.
このかばんはアバカでつくられました。
This bag is made of abaca.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: N1 is made from / of N2.
o: N1 は N2 から・で つくられます
q.e: Use から when the original material changes form (beer from barley), and で when the material is still recognizable (a house made of wood).

points.p: V のは Adj です
points.m: Doing [verb] is [adjective].
points.form: V dictionary form のは Adjective です。
points.note: Add の to the dictionary form of a verb to make it a noun phrase, then comment on it with an adjective such as 難しい, おもしろい or 大変.
ex: バレーボールをするのはむずかしいです。
Playing volleyball is difficult.
バレーボールを見るのはおもしろいです。
Watching volleyball is interesting.
ラッシュに会社にかようのはたいへんです。
Commuting to work during rush hour is hard.
運転しながら、電話するのはあぶないです。
Talking on the phone while driving is dangerous.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Doing [verb] is [adjective].
o: V dictionary form のは Adjective です。
q.e: Add の to the dictionary form of a verb to make it a noun phrase, then comment on it with an adjective such as 難しい, おもしろい or 大変.

points.p: V のが 好き・上手 etc.
points.m: Likes, dislikes and skills related to doing a verb.
points.form: V dictionary form のが Adjective です。
points.note: With 好き, きらい, 上手, 下手, はやい, おそい and similar words, the particle が is used: ～が好き、～がきらい、～が上手、～が下手、～がはやい、～がおそい.
ex: わたしは花をそだてるのが好きです。
I like growing flowers.
わたしはまけるのがきらいです。
I hate to lose.
ポールさんはうそを言うのが下手です。
Paul is not good at telling lies.
パブロさんは朝起きるのが早いです。
Pablo wakes up in the morning early.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Likes, dislikes and skills related to doing a verb.
o: V dictionary form のが Adjective です。
q.e: With 好き, きらい, 上手, 下手, はやい, おそい and similar words, the particle が is used: ～が好き、～がきらい、～が上手、～が下手、～がはやい、～がおそい.

points.p: V のをわすれました
points.m: I forgot to do ~.
points.form: V dictionary form のをわすれました。
points.note: Use the dictionary form of the verb + のを before わすれました to say what you forgot to do.
ex: ドアのかぎをかけるのをわすれました。
I forgot to lock the door.
買い物に行きましたが、ぎゅうにゅうを買うのをわすれました。
I went grocery shopping but I forgot to buy milk.
しゅくだいをしましたが、今日持って来るのをわすれました。
I did my homework, but I forgot to bring it today.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I forgot to do ~.
o: V dictionary form のをわすれました。
q.e: Use the dictionary form of the verb + のを before わすれました to say what you forgot to do.

points.p: V のを知っていますか
points.m: Do you know that ...?
points.form: V plain form のを知っていますか。
points.note: Use the plain form of a verb (including past and passive forms) before のを to ask whether someone knows a fact.
ex: マリアさんに赤ちゃんが生まれたのを知っていますか。
Do you know that Maria had a baby?
ガウトさんが来月けっこんするのを知っていますか。
Do you know that Mr. Gauto is going to get married next month?
北川先生が入院しているのを知っていますか。
Do you know that Ms. Kitagawa is in the hospital?
UFOがアメリカで見られたのを知っていますか。
Do you know that a UFO was seen in the US?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Do you know that ...?
o: V plain form のを知っていますか。
q.e: Use the plain form of a verb (including past and passive forms) before のを to ask whether someone knows a fact.

points.m: The one that ... is Noun. / The one that ... is when / where / whose / what?
points.form: V・い-adj plain form / な-adj・N な のは Noun です。
points.note: Turn a sentence into a noun phrase with の and make it the topic. The answer, or the question word, comes at the end before です.
ex: 1年でいちばんいそがしいのは12月です。
The busiest month of the year is December.
父がなくなったのは十年前です。
The time I lost my father is 10 years ago.
わたしがほしいのは日本せいのスキンケアです。
What I want is skin care products made in Japan.
新しいビルができるのはいつですか。
The new building will be finished when?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: The one that ... is Noun. / The one that ... is when / where / whose / what?
o: V・い-adj plain form / な-adj・N な のは Noun です。
q.e: Turn a sentence into a noun phrase with の and make it the topic. The answer, or the question word, comes at the end before です.

points.p: ～ときも・ときや・ときの・ときに
points.m: The moment / time when ...
points.form: ～ときも / ～ときや / ～ときの / ～ときに
points.note: とき can be followed by も, や, の or に, plus the particle から, to talk about the moment or time when something happens.
ex: つかれたときやさびしいとき、家族を思い出す。
I remember my family like when I am tired or lonely.
生まれたときからずっとニューヨークに住んでいます。
I have been living in New York since I was born.
ヨーロッパへはじめて行ったときにいちばん楽しかったです。
When I first went to Europe was the most fun.
そつぎょうしたときの写真をみつけた。
I found pictures of when I graduated.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: The moment / time when ...
o: ～ときも / ～ときや / ～ときの / ～ときに
q.e: とき can be followed by も, や, の or に, plus the particle から, to talk about the moment or time when something happens.

points.m: Because Sentence 1, Sentence 2.
points.form: Vて／Vなくて／い-adj(い)くて／な-adjで、Sentence 2
points.note: Sentence 2 must NOT contain volition (will, orders, invitation, request); use から instead. It often shows a feeling, state or past situation.
ex: じしんのニュースを聞いて、びっくりしました。
I was surprised to hear the earthquake news.
友達が会えなくて、さびしいです。
I'm sad because I can't meet my friends.
むずかしい漢字が多くて、新聞が読めません。
I can't read the newspaper because there are a lot of difficult kanji.
説明がふくざつで、ぜんぜんわかりません。
I can't understand it at all because the explanation is complicated.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Because Sentence 1, Sentence 2.
o: Vて／Vなくて／い-adj(い)くて／な-adjで、Sentence 2
q.e: Sentence 2 must NOT contain volition (will, orders, invitation, request); use から instead. It often shows a feeling, state or past situation.

points.m: Because of (natural phenomena, happenings, events), Sentence 2.
points.form: Nounで、Sentence 2
points.note: Use a noun + で for a cause such as a fire, earthquake, typhoon or illness. The sentence must NOT contain volition (will, orders, invitation, request).
ex: 火事で、家がやけました。
Because of the fire, the house was burned down.
じしんで、ビルがたおれました。
Because of the earthquake, a building collapsed.
たいふうで、しんかんせんが止まりました。
Because of the typhoon, bullet trains have stopped.
病気で、旅行に行けませんでした。
Because of illness, I was not able to go on a trip.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Because of (natural phenomena, happenings, events), Sentence 2.
q.e: Use a noun + で for a cause such as a fire, earthquake, typhoon or illness. The sentence must NOT contain volition (will, orders, invitation, request).

points.m: Because / Since Sentence 1, Sentence 2.
points.form: Plain form ので、Sentence 2　(な-adj／Noun + なので)
points.note: ～ので gives a cause objectively and softens the tone, so it suits gentle reasons, asking permission or excuses. Polite form (～ますので) also works.
ex: タイに２年住んでいたので、タイ語が少し話せます。
I lived in Thailand for two years, so I can speak a little Thai.
今日は主人のたんじょうびなので、ケーキを買って帰ります。
Today is my husband's birthday, so I'll buy a cake and go home.
気分がわるいので、そうたいしてもいいですか。
I'm not feeling well, so can I leave early?
ようじがあるので、お先にしつれいします。
I have something to do. Pardon me for leaving first.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Because / Since Sentence 1, Sentence 2.
o: Plain form ので、Sentence 2　(な-adj／Noun + なので)
q.e: ～ので gives a cause objectively and softens the tone, so it suits gentle reasons, asking permission or excuses. Polite form (～ますので) also works.

points.m: During Verb / Noun ...
points.form: Verb dictionary form／Noun の とちゅうで、Sentence 2
points.note: Use a dictionary-form verb or a noun + の before とちゅうで to say that something happened in the middle of an action or journey.
ex: じつは来るとちゅうで、じこがあって、バスがおくれてしまったんです。
Actually, on my way here there was an accident and the bus was delayed.
マラソンのとちゅうで、あのビルがばくはつした。
That building exploded during the marathon.
スピーチのとちゅうで、はきけがした。
I felt nauseous during the speech.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: During Verb / Noun ...
o: Verb dictionary form／Noun の とちゅうで、Sentence 2
q.e: Use a dictionary-form verb or a noun + の before とちゅうで to say that something happened in the middle of an action or journey.

points.m: Embeds a question (what, when, which, how much ...) as a clause in a larger sentence.
points.form: Interrogative + V／adj／N plain form か、Sentence
points.note: Put a question word with a plain-form verb, adjective or noun, then か, and continue the sentence. Use it with verbs like 知っている, わからない, おぼえている, かんがえる, しらべる.
ex: 先生は何と言ったか、おぼえていません。
I don't remember what the teacher said.
ゴッホの絵はいくらで売れたか、知っていますか。
Do you know how much the Gogh's painting was sold for?
ミーティングはいつがいいか、考えてください。
Please think about when is a good time for a meeting.
この紙はどちらが表か、わかりません。
I don't know which is the front side of this paper.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Embeds a question (what, when, which, how much ...) as a clause in a larger sentence.
q.e: Put a question word with a plain-form verb, adjective or noun, then か, and continue the sentence. Use it with verbs like 知っている, わからない, おぼえている, かんがえる, しらべる.

points.m: Whether or not ...
points.form: V／adj／N plain form + かどうか、Sentence
points.note: Use かどうか with a yes/no question that is placed inside a sentence. Verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives and nouns all take the plain form.
ex: カードをもうしこむとき、はんこがひつようかどうか、教えてください。
Please tell me whether a hanko is necessary or not when I apply for the card.
にもつの重さが２０キロいかどうか、はかってください。
Please measure whether the weight of the package is less than 20 kilos or not.
道がこんでいて、間にあうかどうか、わかりません。
The street is congested, so I don't know whether we'll make it on time.
さあ、おいしいかどうか、わからない。
Well, I don't know whether it's good or not. I haven't eaten there before.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Whether or not ...
o: V／adj／N plain form + かどうか、Sentence
q.e: Use かどうか with a yes/no question that is placed inside a sentence. Verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives and nouns all take the plain form.

points.m: Try to do Verb (and see how it goes).
points.form: V て-form みます。
points.note: Use the て-form of a verb + みます to try something and see how it turns out.
ex: もういちど考えてみます。
I'll try to think it over again.
このズボンをはいてみてもいいですか。
May I try (wear) this pair of trousers?
サイズがあうかどうか、着てみてください。
Please try it on and see whether the size fits or not.
