q.s: Try to do Verb (and see how it goes).
q.e: Use the て-form of a verb + みます to try something and see how it turns out.

points.m: Changes an い-adjective into a noun (weight, height, length ...).
points.form: い-adj (～い) → ～さ
points.note: Drop the final い of the い-adjective and add さ to make a noun that expresses the degree or amount.
ex: 重さは100キロです。
The weight is 100 kilos.
富士山の高さは3776メートルです。
The height of Mt. Fuji is 3,776 meters.
ズボンの長さはだいじょうぶですか。
Is the length of the pants okay?
このシャツの大きさはちょうどいいですね。
The size of this shirt is just right.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Changes an い-adjective into a noun (weight, height, length ...).
q.e: Drop the final い of the い-adjective and add さ to make a noun that expresses the degree or amount.

points.m: A softer, more polite way of saying ～ですか.
points.form: ～でしょうか。
points.note: The speaker is wondering and asking in a more polite tone. ～でしょうか is also used in polite offers such as いかがでしょうか.
ex: はるちゃんは学校でどうでしょうか？ちょっとしんぱいです。
I'm wondering how Haru-chan is doing at school? I'm a little worried.
じけんについて何か知っているでしょうか？
I'm wondering if you know anything about the incident?
お飲み物はいかがでしょうか？
Would you like something to drink?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: A softer, more polite way of saying ～ですか.
q.e: The speaker is wondering and asking in a more polite tone. ～でしょうか is also used in polite offers such as いかがでしょうか.

points.p: やります／さしあげます
points.m: Give to ~
points.form: Receiver に Object を やります／さしあげます
points.note: For lower-status people, animals or plants use やります; for a person あげます is often preferred. さしあげます shows polite respect to the receiver.
ex: わたしは友だちにおみやげをあげました。
I gave a souvenir to my friend.
わたしは社長におみやげをさしあげました。
I gave the president a souvenir.
わたしは犬にえさをやりました。
I gave the dog some food.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Give to ~
o: Receiver に Object を やります／さしあげます
q.e: For lower-status people, animals or plants use やります; for a person あげます is often preferred. さしあげます shows polite respect to the receiver.

points.m: Receive something from a person of higher status.
points.form: Giver に Object を いただきます
points.note: When the speaker receives a thing from a person of higher social status (e.g. 部長, かちょう, 先生), いただきます is used instead of もらいます.
ex: わたしは部長におみやげをいただきました。
I received a souvenir from the manager.
先生にすてきなえはがきをいただきました。
I received a nice picture postcard from my teacher.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Receive something from a person of higher status.
o: Giver に Object を いただきます
q.e: When the speaker receives a thing from a person of higher social status (e.g. 部長, かちょう, 先生), いただきます is used instead of もらいます.

points.m: A person of higher status gives something to the speaker or the speaker's family.
points.form: Giver は・が Object を くださいます
points.note: When a person of higher social status gives the speaker or the speaker's family member something, くださいます is used instead of くれます.
ex: 店長が(わたしに)おかしをくださいました。
The store manager gave me sweets.
かちょうが娘にチョコレートをくださいました。
The department head gave chocolate to my daughter.
フェルナンデスさんがけっこんのおいわいにこのおさらをくださいました。
Mr. Fernandes gave this plate as a wedding gift.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: A person of higher status gives something to the speaker or the speaker's family.
o: Giver は・が Object を くださいます
q.e: When a person of higher social status gives the speaker or the speaker's family member something, くださいます is used instead of くれます.

points.m: Give / do Verb for someone.
points.form: (Receiver に) Verb て-form やります／あげます
points.note: Add the て-form of the verb before やります or あげます to say you did an action for someone. The same giving verbs are used as for objects.
ex: わたしは息子にえほんを読んでやりました。(あげました)
I read a picture book to my son.
わたしは犬をさんぽに連れて行ってやりました。
I took my dog for a walk.
わたしは娘のしゅくだいを見てやりました。(あげました)
I checked my daughter's homework.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Give / do Verb for someone.
o: (Receiver に) Verb て-form やります／あげます
q.e: Add the て-form of the verb before やります or あげます to say you did an action for someone. The same giving verbs are used as for objects.

points.p: ～ていただきます／～てくださいます
points.m: Receive an action from a person of higher status.
points.form: Giver に Verb て-form いただきます／Giver は・が Verb て-form くださいます
points.note: Use ～ていただきます when you receive the action (Giver に). Use ～てくださいます when a higher person does it for you (Giver は・が).
ex: わたしはかちょうにビデオカメラを貸していただきました。
The department chief lent me a video camera.
水谷先生に文法を説明していただきました。
Mr. Mizutani explained the grammar to me.
フェレイラさんが(わたしの)おみまいに来てくださいました。
Mr. Ferreira came to visit me. (wish me well)
明日社長が(わたしを)くうこうまで送ってくださいます。
Tomorrow, the company president will send me to the airport.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Receive an action from a person of higher status.
o: Giver に Verb て-form いただきます／Giver は・が Verb て-form くださいます
q.e: Use ～ていただきます when you receive the action (Giver に). Use ～てくださいます when a higher person does it for you (Giver は・が).

points.m: Will you kindly ...?
points.form: Verb て-form くださいませんか　(くれませんか)
points.note: A polite way to ask someone to do something for you. くださいませんか is the polite form of くれませんか.
ex: よく聞こえませんでしたが、もういちど言ってくださいませんか。
I didn't hear it well, will you kindly say it one more time?
コピーきが動きませんが、ちょっと見てくださいませんか。
The copying machine is not working, could you please take a look?
セーターのサイズをまちがえましたが、とりかえてくださいませんか。
I've got the size of this sweater wrong, may I ask you to exchange it?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Will you kindly ...?
o: Verb て-form くださいませんか　(くれませんか)
q.e: A polite way to ask someone to do something for you. くださいませんか is the polite form of くれませんか.

points.m: As a token of ... / in memory of ...
points.form: Noun に Verb
points.note: Use に after a noun such as おみやげ, おいわい or おみまい to say what the thing is given or bought as.
ex: ロシア旅行のおみやげににんぎょうを買いました。
I bought a doll as a souvenir of the trip to Russia.
おみまいにくだものを持ってきました。
I brought some fruits. (as a consolatory gift to a sick person)
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: As a token of ... / in memory of ...
q.e: Use に after a noun such as おみやげ, おいわい or おみまい to say what the thing is given or bought as.

points.m: In order to Verb ...
points.form: Verb dictionary form ために、Volitional Sentence
points.note: Use the dictionary form of a volitional verb before ために. The second part must express the speaker's will (volition).
ex: べんごしになるためにほうりつを勉強するつもりです。
I will study law in order to become a lawyer.
大学院に入るために会社をやめようと思っています。
I'm thinking of quitting my work to enter grad school.
自分の店を持つためにちょきんしています。
I am saving money in order to have my own shop.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: In order to Verb ...
o: Verb dictionary form ために、Volitional Sentence
q.e: Use the dictionary form of a volitional verb before ために. The second part must express the speaker's will (volition).

points.m: For the sake of Noun ...
points.form: Noun の ために、Volitional Sentence
points.note: Use a noun + の before ために to say what the action is done for. The second part must express volition.
ex: 仕事のために毎週日本語を習っています。
For the sake of my job, I'm taking Japanese lessons every week.
こくさいもんだいのけんきゅうのためにアメリカへりゅうがくします。
I'm going to study in America for International Issues studies.
日本語の勉強のために電子じしょを買うつもりです。
I will buy an electronic dictionary for my Japanese studies.
こどものきょういくのためにたくさんちょきんしなければなりません。
I have to save a lot for my children's education.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: For the sake of Noun ...
o: Noun の ために、Volitional Sentence
q.e: Use a noun + の before ために to say what the action is done for. The second part must express volition.

points.m: So that (hopefully) ...
points.form: Non-volitional Verb dictionary form／Verb ない ように、Volitional Sentence
points.note: Use ように with a non-volitional verb (potential verbs, stative verbs such as わかります, 聞こえます, 見えます, or negative verbs). The speaker hopes to reach the goal by doing a certain action.
ex: 自分の店を持てるようにちょきんしています。
I am saving money so hopefully I am able to have my own shop.
日本語で上手に話せるように毎日勉強しています。
I study every day so hopefully I can speak well in Japanese.
べんごしになるようにほうりつを勉強しています。
I study law so hopefully I will become a lawyer. (hopeful)
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: So that (hopefully) ...
o: Non-volitional Verb dictionary form／Verb ない ように、Volitional Sentence
q.e: Use ように with a non-volitional verb (potential verbs, stative verbs such as わかります, 聞こえます, 見えます, or negative verbs). The speaker hopes to reach the goal by doing a certain action.

points.m: For the purpose of ...
points.form: Verb dictionary form のに／Noun に、～
points.note: Use のに after a verb (に after a noun) with 使います, やくに立ちます, [時間]がかかります, いいです, 便利です or ひつようです to say what something is for.
ex: ふろしきはものをつつむのにやくに立ちます。
Japanese wrapping cloth is useful to wrap things up.
そろばんはけいさんするのに時間がかかります。
It takes time to calculate with an abacus.
ええ、買い物に便利です。
Yeah, it's convenient for shopping.
ええ、旅行に便利です。
Yeah, it's convenient for traveling.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: For the purpose of ...
o: Verb dictionary form のに／Noun に、～
q.e: Use のに after a verb (に after a noun) with 使います, やくに立ちます, [時間]がかかります, いいです, 便利です or ひつようです to say what something is for.

points.m: At least (amount)
points.form: Quantifier は
points.note: Put は after a quantity to show that this is the minimum amount needed or required.
ex: うちを建てるのに、４０００万円はひつようです。
At least forty million yen is required to build the house.
漢字を２０００おぼえるのに、３年はかかります。
It takes at least 3 years to learn 2000 kanji.
東京で一人でせいかつするのに月に２０万円はいります。
It costs at least 200,000 yen a month to live alone in Tokyo.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: At least (amount)
q.e: Put は after a quantity to show that this is the minimum amount needed or required.

points.m: Takes as much as (amount)
points.form: Quantifier も
points.note: Put も after a quantity to show that the amount is large, as much as or as long as that figure.
ex: うちを建てるのに、４０００万円もひつようですか。
Does it take as much as forty million yen to build the house?
漢字を２０００おぼえるのに、３年もかかりますか。
Does it take as long as 3 years to learn 2000 kanji?
東京で一人でせいかつするのに月に２０万円もいります。
It costs as much as 200,000 yen a month to live alone in Tokyo.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Takes as much as (amount)
q.e: Put も after a quantity to show that the amount is large, as much as or as long as that figure.

points.m: Looks / seems like it is going to ... / it is about to ...
points.form: Verb ます(stem) そうです
points.note: Drop ます from the verb and add そうです to say that something looks like it is just about to happen.
ex: もうあかちゃんが生まれそうだから、すぐタクシーをよんでください！
It feels the baby's coming out! Please call a taxi right away.
中東せんそうでガソリンのねだんが上がりそうです。
Looks like the price of gas will increase because of the war in the Middle East.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Looks / seems like it is going to ... / it is about to ...
o: Verb ます(stem) そうです
q.e: Drop ます from the verb and add そうです to say that something looks like it is just about to happen.

points.m: Judging from the appearance, it looks / seems like ...
points.form: い-adj(～い)・な-adj(～な) そうです
points.note: Drop the final い of an い-adjective or the な of a な-adjective and add そうです. For よい the stem changes to よさ (よさそうです). It is also used to describe other people's feelings.
ex: この料理はおいしそうです。
This dish looks delicious.
かのじょはあたまがよさそうです。
She seems smart.
このつくえはじょうぶそうです。
This desk looks strong and durable.
え、一人で住んでいるんですか。さびしそう。
Oh you live alone? That seems lonely.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Judging from the appearance, it looks / seems like ...
o: い-adj(～い)・な-adj(～な) そうです
q.e: Drop the final い of an い-adjective or the な of a な-adjective and add そうです. For よい the stem changes to よさ (よさそうです). It is also used to describe other people's feelings.

points.m: To go somewhere, do something and come back.
points.form: Verb て-form 来ます
points.note: Use the て-form of a verb followed by 来ます to say you will go to do something and then return.
ex: ちょっとコンビニでコーヒーを買って来ます。
I'll just buy a coffee at the convenience store. (then come back)
キッチンからおやつをとって来ますね。
I'm going to get some snacks from the kitchen. (and come back)
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: To go somewhere, do something and come back.
q.e: Use the て-form of a verb followed by 来ます to say you will go to do something and then return.

points.m: To go out and come back.
points.form: 出かけて 来ます
points.note: 出かけて来ます is a set phrase used when you step out for a while and will return soon.
ex: どこへ行くんですか。／ちょっと出かけて来ます。
Where are you going? / I'm going out (and coming back soon).
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: To go out and come back.
q.e: 出かけて来ます is a set phrase used when you step out for a while and will return soon.

points.m: To do something too much, excessively; something is too ...
points.form: Verb (stem)／い-adj(～い)／な-adj(～な) すぎます
points.note: Drop ます from a verb, the final い of an い-adjective or the な of a な-adjective, and add すぎます to say something is too much or excessive.
ex: ニューヨークでのやちんは日本より高すぎます。
Rent in New York is way too expensive than in Japan.
(わたしには)このセーターは大きすぎます。
This sweater is too large. (for me)
テストのもんだいがかんたんすぎる。
The test questions are too easy. (for me)
何回もお金貸してあげたの？やさしすぎるよ。
You lent him money many times? You are too kind.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: To do something too much, excessively; something is too ...
o: Verb (stem)／い-adj(～い)／な-adj(～な) すぎます
q.e: Drop ます from a verb, the final い of an い-adjective or the な of a な-adjective, and add すぎます to say something is too much or excessive.

points.m: Something is easy / difficult to Verb.
points.form: Verb ます(stem) やすいです／にくいです
points.note: Drop ます and add やすい or にくい. It also says that something will or won't easily happen. The result behaves like an い-adjective (飲みやすくなります).
ex: このアプリは使いやすいです。
This (phone) app is easy to use.
先生の説明はわかりやすいです。
The teacher's explanation is easy to understand.
はしでは食べにくいです。
It's hard to eat with chopsticks.
雪の日は道がよくすべりやすいです。
On snowy days, it's easy to slip on the roads.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Something is easy / difficult to Verb.
o: Verb ます(stem) やすいです／にくいです
q.e: Drop ます and add やすい or にくい. It also says that something will or won't easily happen. The result behaves like an い-adjective (飲みやすくなります).

points.m: To turn something into a certain state.
points.form: い-adj(～い) → く ／ な-adj・Noun に + します
points.note: Change an い-adjective to ～く, or add に to a な-adjective or noun, then use します. Compare ～くなります (something becomes) with ～くします (somebody makes it so).
ex: 前がみがもう長いですから、少し短くしてください。
My bangs are already long, please make it short a little.
ちょっと待って、部屋をきれいにします。
Wait a moment, I'll just tidy up my room.
ごはんのりょうは多すぎるから、半分にしてください。
The amount of rice is too much, please cut it in half.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: To turn something into a certain state.
o: い-adj(～い) → く ／ な-adj・Noun に + します
q.e: Change an い-adjective to ～く, or add に to a な-adjective or noun, then use します. Compare ～くなります (something becomes) with ～くします (somebody makes it so).

points.m: I will have / select / take ~ (expresses selection or decision).
points.form: Noun にします
points.note: Use Noun + にします to say what you choose or decide on, such as an item on a menu or a room type.
ex: 部屋はシングルにしますか、ツインにしますか。
Would you like a single room or a twin room?
シングルにします。
I'll have the single room.
ランチは何にしましょうか。
What shall we have for lunch?
昨日和食を食べたから、今日ようしょくにしましょうよ。
We had Japanese food yesterday, so let's have western food today.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I will have / select / take ~ (expresses selection or decision).
q.e: Use Noun + にします to say what you choose or decide on, such as an item on a menu or a room type.

points.m: To do something in a certain way.
points.form: い-adj(～い) → く ／ な-adj に + Verb
points.note: Turn the adjective into an adverb with く (い-adj) or に (な-adj) and put it before the verb to say how the action is done.
ex: やさいをこまかく切ってください。
Please cut the vegetables into small pieces.
見たことをくわしくせつめいしてください。
Please explain in detail what you've seen.
もう少ししずかに話しましょう。
Please talk more quietly.
電気や水は大切に使いましょう。
Let's conserve electricity and water.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: To do something in a certain way.
o: い-adj(～い) → く ／ な-adj に + Verb
q.e: Turn the adjective into an adverb with く (い-adj) or に (な-adj) and put it before the verb to say how the action is done.

points.m: In case that ... / If ... happens
points.form: V・い-adj・な-adj な・N の 場合は～
points.note: Use 場合は after the dictionary form, た-form or ない-form of a verb, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の) to describe a situation, followed by what to do in that case.
ex: よやくをキャンセルする場合はいつでもれんらくしてください。
In case you will cancel the reservation, just contact us anytime.
火事が起きた場合はすぐに119に電話してください。
In case there is a fire, call 119 right away.
はんこが見つからない場合はどうしたらいいですか。
In case I can't find my seal, what should I do?
ねつが高い場合はこのくすりを飲んでください。
In case your fever is high, please take this medicine.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: In case that ... / If ... happens
o: V・い-adj・な-adj な・N の 場合は～
q.e: Use 場合は after the dictionary form, た-form or ない-form of a verb, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の) to describe a situation, followed by what to do in that case.

points.m: In case of (an event) ...
points.form: N + の場合は～
points.note: Put の between a noun and 場合は to talk about what to do in the case of that event.
ex: りょうしゅうしょが必要な場合は店の人に言ってください。
In case a receipt is needed, just tell the store staff.
じしんの場合はひじょうぐちからにげてください。
In case of an earthquake, run away through the emergency exit.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: In case of (an event) ...
q.e: Put の between a noun and 場合は to talk about what to do in the case of that event.

points.m: Even though ... / Despite the fact that ...
points.form: V (plain form)・い-adj・な-adj な・N な + のに～
points.note: Use のに to connect two sentences when the result is the opposite of what you would expect. It often carries a feeling of surprise or complaint.
ex: やくそくしたのに、かれは来ませんでした。
He did not come, even though he promised.
ケーキを食べるなと言ったのに、何で食べたの。
Despite the fact that I told you not to eat the cake, why did you still eat it?
お母さんが毎日おべんとうを作ってくれているのに、今日は作らなかった。
My mother makes me bento every day. Today, she didn't.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Even though ... / Despite the fact that ...
o: V (plain form)・い-adj・な-adj な・N な + のに～
q.e: Use のに to connect two sentences when the result is the opposite of what you would expect. It often carries a feeling of surprise or complaint.

points.m: Even though ... (adjective / noun)
points.form: い-adj・な-adj な・N な + のに～
points.note: い-adjectives connect directly to のに, while な-adjectives and nouns take な before のに.
ex: りょうしんがせが高いのに、わたしはせが低いんです。
Although both my parents are tall, I'm short.
高かったのに、この車がよくこしょうします。
Even though it was expensive, this car always breaks down.
いちばん上手なのに、かのじょは一位じゃなかった。
Even though she's the most skilled, she didn't get first place.
今日は休みなのに、仕事をしなければなりません。
Even though today is my day off, I have to work.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Even though ... (adjective / noun)
o: い-adj・な-adj な・N な + のに～
q.e: い-adjectives connect directly to のに, while な-adjectives and nouns take な before のに.

points.p: のに vs が・ても
points.m: Choosing between が (but), ても (even if) and のに (even though)
points.note: が simply contrasts two facts (but). ても means "even if", and のに means "even though" with a feeling of surprise. Use the one that fits the meaning.
ex: この部屋は広いですが、暗いです。
This room is big, but dark.
この家は古いですが、きれいです。
This house is old, but beautiful.
この部屋はまどがたくさんありますが、暗いです。
This room has a lot of windows but it's dark.
この部屋はまどがたくさんあるのに、暗いです。
Even though there are many windows, it's dark.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Choosing between が (but), ても (even if) and のに (even though)
q.e: が simply contrasts two facts (but). ても means "even if", and のに means "even though" with a feeling of surprise. Use the one that fits the meaning.

points.p: V dictionary form + ところです
points.m: I am just about to do ~
points.form: V (dictionary form) + ところです。
points.note: Use the dictionary form of the verb with ところです to say that you are at the point just before an action starts. Example form: 食べる → 食べるところです。
ex: 食べるところです。
I am just about to eat.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I am just about to do ~
q.e: Use the dictionary form of the verb with ところです to say that you are at the point just before an action starts. Example form: 食べる → 食べるところです。

points.p: V ている + ところです
points.m: I am in the middle of doing ~
points.form: V ている-form + ところです。
points.note: Use the ている-form with ところです to say that the action is in progress right now. 今 is often used with it.
ex: 今考えているところです。
Have you decided where you will go on summer vacation? / I'm thinking now.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I am in the middle of doing ~
o: V ている-form + ところです。
q.e: Use the ている-form with ところです to say that the action is in progress right now. 今 is often used with it.

points.p: V た-form + ところです
points.m: I have just done ~ (a moment ago)
points.form: V た-form + ところです。
points.note: Use the た-form with ところです to say that an action has only just finished. たった今 (just now) is often added. After a noun, ところなのです can also be used.
ex: たった今バスが出たところです。
The bus left just now.
バスが出たところなのです。
Why are you still here? / Because the bus just left.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I have just done ~ (a moment ago)
o: V た-form + ところです。
q.e: Use the た-form with ところです to say that an action has only just finished. たった今 (just now) is often added. After a noun, ところなのです can also be used.

points.p: V た-form + ばかりです
points.m: Have just done ~ / just finished ~
points.form: V た-form + ばかりです。
points.note: Use the た-form with ばかりです to say that an action has just finished. It is often used to explain a reason or a result that follows from that.
ex: 起きたばかりですから、しょくよくがありません。
I just woke up, so I don't feel like eating yet.
たいいんしたばかりなので、まだスポーツはできません。
I just got out from the hospital, so I can't play sports yet.
あの二人は去年けっこんしたばかりなのに、もうりこんしてしまいました。
Even though those two just got married last year, they already got a divorce.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Have just done ~ / just finished ~
o: V た-form + ばかりです。
q.e: Use the た-form with ばかりです to say that an action has just finished. It is often used to explain a reason or a result that follows from that.

points.m: It is certain ... / I'm sure ... / supposed to ... / should be ...
points.form: V (plain)・い-adj・な-adj な・N の + はずです。
points.note: Use はずです to say that something is expected to be true based on a reason. Attach it to the plain form, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の).
ex: 一ヶ月ほど旅行に行くと言っていましたので、るすのはずです。
Are your neighbors out? / They said they'll go on a trip for about a month, so I suppose they're not there.
びじゅつを勉強しているから、上手なはずです。
Is Olivia good at drawing? / She is studying art, so I'm sure she is good.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: It is certain ... / I'm sure ... / supposed to ... / should be ...
o: V (plain)・い-adj・な-adj な・N の + はずです。
q.e: Use はずです to say that something is expected to be true based on a reason. Attach it to the plain form, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の).

points.m: I heard (from a source) that ...
points.form: V・い-adj・な-adj だ・N だ (plain form) + そうです。
points.note: Attach そうです to the plain form of a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective (+だ) or noun (+だ) to pass on information you heard from someone or somewhere.
ex: 雨が降るそうです。
I heard that it will rain.
この料理はおいしいそうです。
I heard that this food is delicious.
天気よほうによると、明日はさむくなるそうです。
According to the weather forecast, it will be cold tomorrow.
明日だそうです。
When is the new manager coming? / I heard it's tomorrow.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I heard (from a source) that ...
o: V・い-adj・な-adj だ・N だ (plain form) + そうです。
q.e: Attach そうです to the plain form of a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective (+だ) or noun (+だ) to pass on information you heard from someone or somewhere.

points.p: ～そうです vs ～と言っていました
points.m: I heard that ... (a person or a source said so)
points.form: Plain form + そうです。
points.note: Hearsay そうです can be compared with ～と言っていました (said that ...). Both pass on what someone else said.
ex: ヴィンセントは明日京都へ行くそうです。
I heard that Vincent is going to Kyoto tomorrow.
ヴィンセントは明日京都へ行くと言っていました。
Vincent said that he is going to Kyoto tomorrow.
バリはとてもきれいだそうです。
I heard that Bali is very beautiful.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I heard that ... (a person or a source said so)
q.e: Hearsay そうです can be compared with ～と言っていました (said that ...). Both pass on what someone else said.

points.m: It seems that ... / It looks like ...
points.form: V (plain)・い-adj・な-adj な・N の + ようです。
points.note: Use ようです to give your judgment about something based on what you see or sense. Attach it to the plain form, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の).
ex: 人があつまっていますね。じこのようですね。
Look, there is a crowd. It looks like an accident.
どうもかぜをひいたようだ。
I have a cough and a headache. It seems like I've caught a cold.
電気が消えていますね。もうだれもいないようです。
Lights are off. Seems like no one is here anymore.
料理はおいしいようです。
That restaurant is always so crowded. It seems like the food there is delicious.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: It seems that ... / It looks like ...
o: V (plain)・い-adj・な-adj な・N の + ようです。
q.e: Use ようです to give your judgment about something based on what you see or sense. Attach it to the plain form, an い-adjective, a な-adjective (+な) or a noun (+の).

points.p: な / の + ようです
points.m: It looks like ... (な-adjective / noun)
points.form: な-adj + なようです / N + のようです
points.note: A な-adjective takes な and a noun takes の before ようです.
ex: 田中さんはやさいを食べません。きらいなようです。
Ms Tanaka doesn't eat vegetables. It looks like she doesn't like it.
川田さんは病院に行きました。病気のようです。
Mr. Kawada went to the hospital. It looks like he is sick.
先生はかいぎ中です。そしてテーブルの上にたくさんのしょるいがおいてあります。いそがしいようです。
Teacher is in a meeting and his desk is piled with documents. It seems that he is busy.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: It looks like ... (な-adjective / noun)
o: な-adj + なようです / N + のようです
q.e: A な-adjective takes な and a noun takes の before ようです.

points.m: I hear / smell / taste ~
points.form: 音・こえ・におい・あじ + がします。
points.note: Use がします with 音 (sound), こえ (voice), におい (smell) and あじ (taste) to say that you notice something with your senses.
ex: へんな音がしますね。
There's a strange sound, isn't there?
へんなにおいがしますね。ええ、何かもえているようです。
It smells weird. / Right, it seems something is burning.
へんなあじがするね。しょうゆとソースをまちがえたようです。
It tastes weird. It seems I got the soy sauce and sauce wrong.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: I hear / smell / taste ~
o: 音・こえ・におい・あじ + がします。
q.e: Use がします with 音 (sound), こえ (voice), におい (smell) and あじ (taste) to say that you notice something with your senses.

points.m: make / let someone do something (intransitive verb)
points.form: Person は・が Person を・に Verb (causative form)。
points.note: The person who gives the order (action teller) is the topic or subject, and the person who does the action (action doer) takes を or に before the causative verb.
ex: ぼくは妹をなかせた。
I made my younger sister cry.
先生は子どもたちに自由にあそばせた。
The teacher let the children play freely.
店長はカミロに休ませた。
The store manager let Camilo rest.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: make / let someone do something (intransitive verb)
o: Person は・が Person を・に Verb (causative form)。
q.e: The person who gives the order (action teller) is the topic or subject, and the person who does the action (action doer) takes を or に before the causative verb.

points.m: make / let someone do something (with an object)
points.form: Action Teller は Action Doer に Object を Verb (causative form)。
points.note: When the verb has an object, the action doer is marked with に and the object with を.
ex: 部長は部下に仕事を休ませました。
The manager made/let his staff take time off from work.
先生はせいとに自由にいけんを言わせました。
The teacher let the students freely say their opinion.
父は兄にやりたいことをやらせます。
Dad lets my brother do what he wants to do.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: make / let someone do something (with an object)
o: Action Teller は Action Doer に Object を Verb (causative form)。
q.e: When the verb has an object, the action doer is marked with に and the object with を.

points.m: Verbs of emotion take を for the person made to feel something
points.form: Person を Verb (causative form)
points.note: With emotion verbs (しんぱいする, よろこぶ, かなしむ, おこる), the person who feels it takes を. Also used when telling an outsider that someone in your own group will do something.
ex: 子どものとき、体がよわくて、母をしんぱいさせました。
When I was a child, I made my mother worry because of my poor health.
あなたをかなしませたくない。
I don't want to make you sad.
かかりの者をむかえに行かせます。
When you arrive at the station, please call me. I will send someone to pick you up.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Verbs of emotion take を for the person made to feel something
q.e: With emotion verbs (しんぱいする, よろこぶ, かなしむ, おこる), the person who feels it takes を. Also used when telling an outsider that someone in your own group will do something.

points.m: Would you please let me ...?
points.form: Verb (causative form) て + いただけませんか。
points.note: A polite request asking a person of higher status for permission to do something. Put the verb in the causative form, then add ていただけませんか。
ex: コピーきを使わせていただけませんか。
Would you let me use the copying machine?
ここにしばらく車を止めさせていただけませんか。
Would you let me park my car here for a while? I want to unload the luggage.
気分がわるいので、そうたいさせていただけませんか。
I'm not feeling well, would you please let me leave early?
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Would you please let me ...?
o: Verb (causative form) て + いただけませんか。
q.e: A polite request asking a person of higher status for permission to do something. Put the verb in the causative form, then add ていただけませんか。

points.m: Respectful (sonkeigo) form of a verb
points.form: Subject は・が Verb (れる・られる passive form)
points.note: The passive form of a verb can be used to show respect to the person doing the action. Group 1: 書きます → 書かれます. Group 2: 出ます → 出られます. Group 3: 来ます → 来られます, します → されます.
ex: 書きます → 書かれます
write
出ます → 出られます
go out
来ます → 来られます
come
します → されます
do
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Respectful (sonkeigo) form of a verb
o: Subject は・が Verb (れる・られる passive form)
q.e: The passive form of a verb can be used to show respect to the person doing the action. Group 1: 書きます → 書かれます. Group 2: 出ます → 出られます. Group 3: 来ます → 来られます, します → されます.

points.p: お + stem + になります
points.m: More respectful pattern than the passive form
points.form: Subject は お Verb (stem) になります。
points.note: Put お before the verb stem and add になります. It cannot be used with one-mora verbs (見る, 寝る, 来る, する, 行く) or Group 3 verbs; special verbs are used instead.
ex: この本をお書きになりましたか。
Did you write this book?
かいぎのよていはいつも部長がお決めになります。
The plan for the meeting is always decided by the department head.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: More respectful pattern than the passive form
o: Subject は お Verb (stem) になります。
q.e: Put お before the verb stem and add になります. It cannot be used with one-mora verbs (見る, 寝る, 来る, する, 行く) or Group 3 verbs; special verbs are used instead.

points.m: Special verbs that replace the normal verb
points.form: Subject は・が Special respectful verb
points.note: Some verbs have their own respectful form: いらっしゃいます (go / come / exist), おっしゃいます (say), めしあがります (eat / drink), ごらんになります (see), なさいます (do), ごぞんじです (know).
ex: 社長はぼうねんかいが来週になったことをごぞんじですか。
Does the president know the year-end party was moved to next week?
せいひんをごらんになりますか。
Would you like to see our products?
昨夜ゆっくりお休みになれましたか。
Could you sleep well last night?
着物をおめしになっている方は坂本さんです。
The person wearing a kimono is Ms. Sakamoto.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Special verbs that replace the normal verb
o: Subject は・が Special respectful verb
q.e: Some verbs have their own respectful form: いらっしゃいます (go / come / exist), おっしゃいます (say), めしあがります (eat / drink), ごらんになります (see), なさいます (do), ごぞんじです (know).

points.p: なさいます・くださいます・いらっしゃいます
points.m: How long did you ~ / gave me / will he come
points.form: Subject は・が Special respectful verb
points.note: なさいます and くださいます are used for する and くれる, and いらっしゃいます also works in plain keigo (いらっしゃるの, いらっしゃらない).
ex: どのぐらい日本語を勉強なさいましたか。
How long did you study Japanese?
先生が本をくださいました。
Teacher gave me a book.
デシアンさんはぼうねんかいにいらっしゃいますか。
Will Mr. De Cyan be coming to the year-end party?
いいえ、いらっしゃらないと思います。
No, I don't think he'll come.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: How long did you ~ / gave me / will he come
o: Subject は・が Special respectful verb
q.e: なさいます and くださいます are used for する and くれる, and いらっしゃいます also works in plain keigo (いらっしゃるの, いらっしゃらない).

points.m: Respectful way of asking someone to do something
points.form: Subject は お Verb (stem) ください。
points.note: A respectful way to ask someone to do something. It cannot be used with the special verbs above, except for eat and look (おめしあがりください, ごらんください).
ex: どうぞおめしあがりください。
Please help yourself.
どうぞごらんください。
Please take a look.
こちらにお名前とご住所をお書きください。
Please write your name and address here.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Respectful way of asking someone to do something
o: Subject は お Verb (stem) ください。
q.e: A respectful way to ask someone to do something. It cannot be used with the special verbs above, except for eat and look (おめしあがりください, ごらんください).

points.m: Respectful form of nouns, adjectives and adverbs
points.form: お + word of Japanese origin / ご + word of Chinese origin
points.note: お is attached to words of Japanese origin and ご to words of Chinese origin. Keep the keigo level consistent within a sentence.
ex: お国、お名前、お仕事、お水、お茶、お金
お is used with Japanese-origin words (Japanese: country / name / work / water / tea / money)
ご家族、ご意見、ご旅行、ご注意、ご案内、ご両親
ご is used with Chinese-origin words (family / opinion / trip / caution / guide / parents)
お元気、お上手、ご熱心、ご親切、ご自由に、ごゆっくり
Adjectives and adverbs
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Respectful form of nouns, adjectives and adverbs
o: お + word of Japanese origin / ご + word of Chinese origin
q.e: お is attached to words of Japanese origin and ご to words of Chinese origin. Keep the keigo level consistent within a sentence.

points.m: Humble speech for Group 1 and 2 verbs
points.form: お Verb (stem) します
points.note: Humble speech lowers your own action. To an outsider (外の人), your own family, company and friends count as insiders, so humble forms are used for their actions too.
ex: 兄が車でお送りします。
My older brother will take you in his car.
お茶をお入れします。
I'll pour you some tea.
ボールペンをお貸しします。
I'll lend you a pen.
points.importanceReason: Equal priority: no source importance ranking supplied

q.s: Humble speech for Group 1 and 2 verbs
q.e: Humble speech lowers your own action. To an outsider (外の人), your own family, company and friends count as insiders, so humble forms are used for their actions too.

points.m: Humble speech for Group 3 verbs
points.form: ご Verb します
points.note: Use ご with Group 3 verbs. Exceptions take お instead: お電話します (call) and おやくそくします (promise). お帰りします is not used for "I'm going home".
ex: (someone)にお電話します
Call (someone)
(someone)をごしょうかいします
Introduce (someone)
(someone)をごしょうたいします
Invite (someone)

q.s: Humble speech for Group 3 verbs
q.e: Use ご with Group 3 verbs. Exceptions take お instead: お電話します (call) and おやくそくします (promise). お帰りします is not used for "I'm going home".

points.m: Special verbs that replace the normal verb
points.form: Subject は Special humble verb
points.note: Some verbs have their own humble form, for example おります (be), まいります / うかがいます (go / come), もうします (say), いただきます (receive / eat / drink), はいけんします (see) and いたします (do).

Do you know the name of the man who spoke at the meeting? / Yes, I do.

q.s: Special verbs that replace the normal verb

points.m: Polite equivalent of です
points.form: Noun・Adjective + でございます

points.m: Polite equivalent of いいですか
points.form: ～ても よろしいでしょうか。
points.note: Use よろしいでしょうか in place of いいですか when you ask for permission politely.
ex: このパンフレットをいただいてもよろしいでしょうか。
May I have one of these pamphlets? / Yes, go ahead.

q.s: Polite equivalent of いいですか
o: ～ても よろしいでしょうか。

ordering.s: わたしは ＿＿ ＿＿ ＿★＿ ＿＿ いきます。
ordering.e: ともだちと いっしょに えいがを みに いきます。 = I'm going with a friend to see a movie. (みに = purpose of going)

ordering.s: きのうは ＿＿ ＿＿ ＿★＿ ＿＿ いました。
ordering.e: あめが ふって いたので うちに いました。 = It was raining, so I stayed home.

ordering.s: この ほんは ＿＿ ＿＿ ＿★＿ ＿＿ です。
ordering.e: すこし むずかしい けど おもしろい です。 = It's a little difficult, but interesting.
